title: Engaging way to trade with AI
author: LazarB33
selftext:
Hello everyone,  
My cousin (who is a professional trader) and I have spent some time building an interactive AI trading floor that will both help you trade and make it engaging. He was working on it for some time and I made a bet with him that if I made a trailer, and post it on social media we will get some sign ups (link below).

So let me tell you more about the platform. Basically you manage your own trading floor on Wall Street full of AI agents. You have your main assistant: Taurus, that will help you with your trading performance. You can spawn trading agents that let you turn any strategy into a bot that trades for you. Our goal is to turn every possible strategy into a deterministic outcome that will be traded with pre-set rules. We made this possible by having our own script tool that allows the AI to write on it and make strategies and indicators for everything. You also have a social aspect that will allow you to either share or sell your trading agents on our marketplace. Or if you want to do trading by yourself and just use the AI as assistant, you can do that with our charting tool and add your trading setups, and let our AI be more personalised for you, by learning what type of trader you are. You also get access to our other features such as research agent that does research on strategies that will work for you or our news agent that is also personalised for you and provides you with news that will matter for you.

This is just an early preview. If you are interested consider signing up for the waitlist to get early access and test our platform. Also consider answering our questionnaire. Any feedback is appreciated! Thank you!

[https://soleatrading.com/](https://soleatrading.com/)

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: rules can be deterministic, outcomes can't. before a spawned bot goes live, what does the user see, a backtest with real fills or only the chart the AI drew?

replies.author: LazarB33
replies.body: Correct, deterministic rules not outcome, what I meant is that you have pre-set rules that the bot follows and not leaving to an LLM to make decisions. Before a spawned bot goes live you get backtest of the strategy, whether it would’ve been stopped out in the past and you get recommendations on what you can tweak to improve it, only then you decide whether to launch the bot or not.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: got it, the LLM writes the rules and then stays out of the loop. that's the sane split. the "would it have been stopped out" check is only as good as its fills though, a stop filled at the stop price on a gap open makes every backtest look better than it was.

replies.author: LazarB33
replies.body: Yes, that's a classic trap, but our backtester is designed to fill at the opening price, not the stop price.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: filling at the open on a gap through the stop is the honest version, good. the one that still bites after that is a single bar that touches both the stop and the target, the backtest has to pick an order and the default pick is usually the flattering one.

replies.author: LazarB33
replies.body: We specifically designed it to assume the stop happened first. Imo better to undersell it and then be surprised by the results, than the opposite.

comments.author: Elegant-Conflict3910
comments.body: Is this just built on top of Paperclip? It seems like it is with the whole chief of staff and hiring system.

replies.author: LazarB33
replies.body: No, it's not built on Paperclip or any agent framework. Solea is its own software.
